name: shop-api
message: The manifest sets no namespace, so the object goes to the namespace of the current context, which is often default.
fix: Set metadata.namespace, or apply the files with a namespace on the command line and keep that in the pipeline.

name: shop-api
message: The Deployment runs one replica, and no PodDisruptionBudget in the files selects its Pods. A voluntary disruption, such as draining a node, takes the only Pod down.
fix: Run two or more replicas and add a PodDisruptionBudget, or accept the downtime on purpose.

name: shop-api
message: hostNetwork is true, so the Pod shares the host's namespace. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards disallows it.
fix: Remove hostNetwork, or set it to false.

name: shop-api
message: The container has no resource request for cpu and memory. The scheduler cannot place it by what it needs, and the node can evict it first when memory runs short.
fix: Set resources.requests.cpu and resources.requests.memory to what the container uses in normal work.

name: shop-api
message: The container has no resource limit for cpu and memory, so nothing stops it from using more of it than it asked for.
fix: Set resources.limits.memory (and resources.limits.cpu if you want a ceiling on CPU).

name: shop-api
message: The container has no readinessProbe (it has a livenessProbe, which does not wait for readiness), so the Pod receives traffic as soon as it starts, before the application can answer.
fix: Add a readinessProbe (httpGet, tcpSocket, grpc or exec) that succeeds only when the application can answer.

name: shop-api
message: The image registry.example/shop/api:latest uses the tag latest. Kubernetes cannot tell which version of the image is running, and a rollback does not return to the version before.
fix: Use a tag that names a version, or the digest of the image (name@sha256:...).

name: shop-api
message: The container binds the port of the node 8080 with hostPort. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards says host ports should be disallowed entirely, or restricted to a known list.
fix: Remove hostPort and reach the container through a Service.

name: shop-api
message: The environment variable DATABASE_PASSWORD is written in the manifest with a plain value, and its name says it holds a secret. The value is not shown here.
fix: Keep the value in a Secret and read it with valueFrom.secretKeyRef.

name: shop-api
message: allowPrivilegeEscalation is not set to false. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards allows only false.
fix: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false.

name: shop-api
message: runAsNonRoot is not set to true, on the container or on the Pod. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards requires containers to run as non-root users.
fix: Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot to true, on the container or on the Pod, and make sure the image runs as a user other than root.

name: shop-api
message: No seccomp profile is set, on the container or on the Pod. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards says that the absence of a profile is prohibited.
fix: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault (or Localhost).

name: shop-api
message: The container runs privileged. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards disallows it.
fix: Remove privileged, or set it to false, and add only the capabilities the container needs.

name: shop-api
message: The container does not drop ALL capabilities. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards says containers must drop ALL capabilities.
fix: Set securityContext.capabilities.drop to [ALL], and add back only what the container needs.

name: shop-api
message: The container adds SYS_ADMIN, which the Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards does not list among the capabilities that may be added.
fix: Remove these capabilities, or run the workload in a namespace that enforces the Privileged profile on purpose.

name: shop-api
message: The image registry.example/shop/log-shipper has no tag and no digest, so Kubernetes uses the tag latest.
fix: Use a tag that names a version, or the digest of the image (name@sha256:...).

name: shop-worker
message: runAsUser of the Pod is 0, which is root. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards does not allow it.
fix: Set runAsUser to a user id above 0.

name: shop-worker
message: The volume spool is a hostPath volume, which mounts a path of the node into the Pod. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards forbids it.
fix: Use a persistentVolumeClaim, a configMap, a secret or an emptyDir instead of a path of the node.
